{{Short description|In mathematics, a mapping between categories}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''direct image functor''' describes how structured data assigned to one space can be systematically transferred to another space using a continuous map between them. More precisely, if we have a [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]]—an object that encodes data like functions or sections over open regions—defined on a space ''X'', and a [[continuous map]] from ''X'' to another space ''Y'', then the direct image functor produces a corresponding sheaf on ''Y''. This construction is a central tool in sheaf theory and is widely used in [[topology]] and [[algebraic geometry]] to relate local data across spaces.

More formally, given a sheaf ''F'' defined on a [[topological space]] ''X'' and a [[continuous map]] ''f'': ''X'' → ''Y'', we can define a new sheaf ''f''<sub>∗</sub>''F'' on ''Y'', called the '''direct image sheaf''' or the '''pushforward sheaf''' of ''F'' along ''f'', such that the global sections of ''f''<sub>∗</sub>''F'' is given by the global sections of ''F''. This assignment gives rise to a [[functor]] ''f''<sub>∗</sub> from the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of sheaves on ''X'' to the category of sheaves on ''Y'', which is known as the direct image functor. Similar constructions exist in many other algebraic and geometric contexts, including that of [[quasi-coherent sheaves]] and [[Étale sheaf|étale sheaves]] on a [[Scheme (mathematics)|scheme]].
{{Images of sheaves}}

==Definition==
Let ''f'': ''X'' → ''Y'' be a continuous map of topological spaces, and let Sh(–) denote the category of sheaves of [[abelian group]]s on a topological space. The direct image functor  

:<math>f_*: \operatorname{Sh}(X) \to \operatorname{Sh}(Y)</math>

sends a sheaf ''F'' on ''X'' to its direct image presheaf ''f''<sub>∗</sub>''F'' on ''Y'', defined on open subsets ''U'' of ''Y'' by

:<math>f_*F(U) := F(f^{-1}(U)).</math>

This turns out to be a sheaf on ''Y'', and is called the direct image sheaf or pushforward sheaf of ''F'' along ''f''.  

Since a [[morphism of sheaves]] φ: ''F'' → ''G'' on ''X'' gives rise to a morphism of sheaves ''f''<sub>∗</sub>(φ): ''f''<sub>∗</sub>(''F'') → ''f''<sub>∗</sub>(''G'') on ''Y'' in an obvious way, we indeed have that ''f''<sub>∗</sub> is a functor.

=== Example ===
If ''Y'' is a point, and ''f'': ''X'' → ''Y'' the unique continuous map, then Sh(''Y'') is the category '''Ab''' of abelian groups, and the direct image functor ''f''<sub>∗</sub>: Sh(''X'') → '''Ab''' equals the [[global sections functor]].

=== Variants ===
If dealing with sheaves of sets instead of sheaves of abelian groups, the same definition applies. Similarly, if ''f'': (''X'', ''O<sub>X</sub>'') → (''Y'', ''O<sub>Y</sub>'') is a morphism of [[ringed space]]s, we obtain a direct image functor ''f''<sub>∗</sub>: Sh(''X'',''O<sub>X</sub>'') → Sh(''Y'',''O<sub>Y</sub>'') from the category of sheaves of ''O<sub>X</sub>''-modules to the category of sheaves of ''O<sub>Y</sub>''-modules. Moreover, if ''f'' is now a morphism of [[Quasi-compact morphism|quasi-compact]] and [[Quasi-separated morphism|quasi-separated]] schemes, then ''f''<sub>∗</sub> preserves the property of being quasi-coherent, so we obtain the direct image functor between categories of quasi-coherent sheaves.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Section 26.24 (01LA): Functoriality for quasi-coherent modules—The Stacks project |url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LA |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=stacks.math.columbia.edu}}</ref>

A similar definition applies to sheaves on [[topos|topoi]], such as [[Étale topology|étale sheaves]]. There, instead of the above preimage ''f''<sup>−1</sup>(''U''), one uses the [[fiber product]] of ''U'' and ''X'' over ''Y''.

== Properties ==
* Forming sheaf categories and direct image functors itself defines a functor from the category of topological spaces to the category of categories: given continuous maps ''f'': ''X'' → ''Y'' and ''g'': ''Y'' → ''Z'', we have (''gf'')<sub>∗</sub>=''g''<sub>∗</sub>''f''<sub>∗</sub>.
* The direct image functor is [[adjoint functor|right adjoint]] to the [[inverse image functor]], which means that for any continuous <math>f: X \to Y</math> and sheaves <math>\mathcal F, \mathcal G</math> respectively on ''X'', ''Y'', there is a natural isomorphism:
:<math>\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf {Sh}(X)}(f^{-1} \mathcal G, \mathcal F ) = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf {Sh}(Y)}(\mathcal G, f_*\mathcal F)</math>.
* If ''f'' is the inclusion of a closed subspace ''X'' ⊆ ''Y'' then ''f''<sub>∗</sub> is [[exact functor|exact]]. Actually, in this case ''f''<sub>∗</sub> is an [[equivalence of categories|equivalence]] between the category of sheaves on ''X'' and the category of sheaves on ''Y'' supported on ''X''. This follows from the fact that the stalk of <math>(f_* \mathcal F)_y</math> is <math>\mathcal F_y</math> if <math>y \in X</math> and zero otherwise (here the closedness of ''X'' in ''Y'' is used).
* If ''f'' is the morphism of affine schemes <math>\mathrm{Spec} \, S \to \mathrm{Spec} \, R</math> determined by a ring homomorphism <math>\phi: R \to S</math>, then the direct image functor ''f''<sub>∗</sub> on quasi-coherent sheaves identifies with the [[restriction of scalars]] functor along φ.

== Higher direct images ==
{{See also|Coherent duality}}

The direct image functor is [[exact functor|left exact]], but usually not right exact. Hence one can consider the right [[derived functor]]s of the direct image. They are called '''higher direct images''' and denoted ''R<sup>q</sup> f''<sub>∗</sub>.

One can show that there is a similar expression as above for higher direct images: for a sheaf ''F'' on ''X'', the sheaf ''R<sup>q</sup> f''<sub>∗</sub>(''F'') is the sheaf associated to the presheaf
:<math>U \mapsto H^q(f^{-1}(U), F)</math>,
where ''H<sup>q</sup>'' denotes [[sheaf cohomology]].

In the context of algebraic geometry and a morphism <math>f: X \to Y</math> of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, one likewise has the right derived functor

:<math>Rf_*: D_{qcoh}(X) \to D_{qcoh}(Y)</math>

as a functor between the (unbounded) [[derived categories]] of quasi-coherent sheaves. In this situation, <math>Rf_*</math> always admits a right adjoint <math>f^{\times}</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Section 48.3 (0A9D): Right adjoint of pushforward—The Stacks project |url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A9D |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=stacks.math.columbia.edu}}</ref> This is closely related, but not generally equivalent to, the [[exceptional inverse image functor]] <math>f^!</math>, unless <math>f</math> is also [[Proper morphism|proper]].
